sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the scope of the exclusionary rule. It tests whether a good-faith administrative mistake by police warrants suppressing evidence. The core issue is the balance between deterring misconduct and admitting probative evidence.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the evidence admitted because the police error was isolated and good-faith.
The government wants the evidence excluded to deter future police recordkeeping failures.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the exclusionary rule should not apply to isolated, good-faith administrative errors.
The government argues the rule must deter all police misconduct, regardless of the error's nature.
